title: Stop getting attacked
problem: Every rally seems to end with somebody smashing a ball at you. It feels like they are just better, or hitting harder — but the ball they attacked was one you gave them.
outcome: You stop feeding attackable balls, and when one does come at you, you have something to do about it other than flinch.

steps.why: Standing too deep turns ordinary dinks into half-volleys off your shoelaces, and a half-volley pops up. A lot of what feels like being attacked starts here.
The shot that denies them anything to hit. Low, short, unattackable — that is the whole job.
A dink with no pace on it gives them nothing to borrow. They have to generate everything themselves, which is where their mistakes come from.
The one that saves you when it has already gone wrong. It turns a ball being driven at you back into a dinking rally.
For the speed-up you did not see coming. Both answers start from the same ready position, and having one is what stops the flinch.
Good players aim at the shoulder of your paddle arm on purpose. This is the one body position that has to be practised rather than reacted to.
